event_summary: Unclassified 1.8-second spectral transient at T+04:17:32 coinciding with a 41% increase in radiation counter readings and 2 checksum errors.

preservation_priorities.reason: Primary instrument data required to analyze the nature of the transient.
preservation_priorities.consequence_if_lost: Loss of primary spectral evidence prevents distinguishing between a real event and an SEU.

preservation_priorities.reason: Necessary to establish temporal correlation with the spectrometer transient.
preservation_priorities.consequence_if_lost: Unable to confirm if the radiation increase was concurrent or coincident noise.

preservation_priorities.reason: Provides evidence of data integrity issues coinciding with the event.
preservation_priorities.consequence_if_lost: Unable to determine if checksum errors are related to the transient or unrelated noise.

preservation_priorities.reason: Used to rule out bus voltage fluctuations as a cause for the transient.
preservation_priorities.consequence_if_lost: Loss of ability to rule out power-induced instrument glitches.
Minimal impact on primary hypothesis differentiation.

recommended_follow_up: Perform a spectrometer calibration check to ensure no permanent degradation occurred following the transient.
compression_warning: The command SET_COMPRESSION_MODE HIGH was issued shortly before the event. Temporal averaging or lossy compression of the radiation_window will destroy sub-second timing information, making it impossible to establish the 0-200ms lead time required to confirm a genuine external radiation event.
uncertainty_statement: It is currently undetermined whether the spectral transient was caused by a physical external particle event, an internal SEU in the ADC, or data corruption indicated by the checksum errors. Temporal correlation between the spectrometer and radiation counter is required for differentiation.

source_references.relevance: Identifies ADC susceptibility to SEUs producing spurious spikes.
Links 41% radiation increase to external particle events.
Warns against temporal averaging of radiation data.
Defines the 0-200ms temporal offset for genuine radiation events.
Provides priority order for evidence preservation.
